> Jack / team — attaching a worked example and the channel margin workbook. Summary here to make it easy: 
>
> Scenario A (list-price uplift):
> - List price per 1k tokens: $0.12
> - Reseller uplift 12% applied to list -> partner sees $0.0132 on top of list
> - Customer discount applied downstream; partner margin appears as an inflated list that can complicate your internal reporting
>
> Scenario B (post-discount carve-out — recommended):
> - Start with gross customer price after customer discount
> - Carve out 12% of net revenue to partner (this is what we remit to the reseller)
> - Effective unit economics are cleaner for your finance team and aligns with how most hyperscalers treat partner pass-throughs>
>
> I attached redwood-channel-margin-workback.xlsx with both tabs and a simple pivot so you can drop in your forecast and see the net-back.
>
> If Acme prefers roll-forward credits we model a small deferred liability and allocate it against unused credits for up to 90 days. That increases near-term breakage assumptions by ~0.6% in our model — not material but worth noting.
